chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ash'ari from Imran ibn Musa from Abu al-Hasan Dawud ibn Muhammad al-Nahdi from Ali ibn Ja'far from Abu al-Hasan al-Tayyeb, who said: I heard him saying:

When Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) entered the market and bought a dog, a ram, and a rooster. When the informant wrote to Harun al-Rashid about this, he said, 'We are secure from his side.' Then Az-Zubayri wrote that Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him) had opened his door and was inviting people to himself. Harun said, 'How strange is this man! He writes that Ali ibn Musa bought a dog, a rooster, and a ram, and now he writes this stuff about him!'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) buy in the market and how did Harun al-Rashid react to the reports about it?
ai.summary: This narrative illustrates the strategic political maneuvering of Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) during the reign of Harun al-Rashid, utilizing the 'buying a dog' incident as a calculated ruse to lower the Caliph's guard against his growing influence. While Harun was bewildered by the apparent contradiction between the Imam's modest market purchases and his active public engagement, Shia scholars view this as a deliberate display of humility and accessibility that masked his true status as the designated successor. The episode highlights the tension between Abbasid suspicion and the Imam's quiet consolidation of authority through social presence rather than overt political challenge.
